items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The owner manager was a Mr. Johhny Powell... We started working there on a percentage basis because Johnny Powell could not afford to pay a regular salary.

ctx.x: The next few days were real rough because my money was very short and so was that of Mack Walker. We were real buddies and shared what ever money we had between us. We could manage only one hot meal a day, so we ate sweet rolls which we could get 10 for 15 cents in a bakery. That was our breakfast which we had around one or two o'clock in the afternoon, and we ate a hot meal for 25 cents with coffee, tea or milk in a big cafeteria on 8th Avenue not far from where we lived.

After one week of eating in this manner, Lloyd came around and told us that he had a job for us in a cabaret for the rest of the month in January. The name of the place was the Capitol at 140th Street and Lenox Avenue under a big Chinese restaurant. Lloyd had played in the Capitol with a famous orchestra. The owner manager was a Mr. Johhny Powell and the cabaret had been one of the most popular clubs in Harlem.

We started working there on a percentage basis because Johnny Powell could not afford to pay a regular salary. The Capitol had lost its popalaty and business was not good, but Johnny was trying to keep the place going in hope that it would become popular again. We had to play behind a couple of women singers who's names I don't remember. They went from table to table when ever there were enough people for them to sing to.
